heroHeadline: Artemis Accords Reach 67 Nations as Paraguay Signs May 7 — IFT-12 Slips to NET May 15 After Booster 19 Static Fire Abort
heroSubtitle: May 7–8: Paraguay became the 67th Artemis Accords signatory at a ceremony in Asunción on May 7, the fourth new nation in nine days (Morocco April 29, Malta and Ireland May 4, Paraguay May 7), driven by international momentum from Artemis II's successful crewed lunar flyby (April 1–10). Indonesia is publicly weighing a potential signature as the 68th nation (Jakarta Post, May 8). At Starbase, SpaceX's IFT-12 has slipped to NET May 15 (from the original May 12 opening window) after a Booster 19 static fire abort caused by a ramp manifold sensor anomaly — all 33 Raptor engines were already replaced following a partial-damage Apr 15 fire, and a follow-up static fire is needed before the FAA-approved launch can proceed. The May 12–18 window has shifted to May 15–18. IFT-12 remains the critical next step to validate Starship docking port and propellant-transfer hardware for Artemis III HLS qualification. At Kennedy Space Center, day 28 post-Artemis II splashdown operations continue: Orion heat shield visual inspection at the Multi-Payload Processing Facility is advancing; formal X-ray scans remain scheduled at Marshall Space Flight Center for summer 2026. Artemis III SLS core stage integration progresses in the VAB. The Artemis II crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) continue week-5 physiological reconditioning at JSC.
